Subject: POC capacity planning - NovaTech (reserved GPUs / autoscale)

Hi Samira / Oliver,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the 2 proof-of-concept (Search Assist and Customer Summaries) workloads and the success criteria you shared. To keep momentum, summary + a first-cut capacity plan below so we can align on sizing and timelines.

Quick summary of success criteria you called out:
- Search Assist: 95th p99 latency < 300ms for top-10 queries at target QPS; sustained throughput for batch re-ranks (up to 10k docs/night).
- Customer Summaries: 95% summary accuracy against your internal eval set; end-to-end latency < 2s for single-customer summary.

Workload notes (from your perf notes):
- Search Assist: mostly short prompts, average token length ~ 40, peak QPS expected 80 with burst to 200 for demo spikes.
- Customer Summaries: longer inputs (avg 1200 tokens), concurrent requests typically 10-20 during demo windows.

First-cut capacity proposal:
- Reserved capacity: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs for the duration of the POC (4 weeks) as the baseline. This supports sustained Search Assist QPS ~80 and parallel summary jobs.
- Autoscaling / burst: configure burst pool with up to 6x A100-equivalents (on-demand) for demo days. Billed via committed + burst model; burst has higher per-hour rate.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for Search Assist to reduce repeated token compute; we estimate 20-30% token cost reduction based on query distribution.

Suggested timeline:
- Week 0 (next 3 business days): sign POC SOW + confirm cloud region and VPC peering.
- Week 1: infra provisioned, baseline model pinned (open model candidate), run smoke tests.
- Week 2-3: load tests and tuning (autoscale thresholds, batching config).
- Week 4: acceptance testing against your eval set; retro + recommendation.

Ownership:
- Redwood: infra provisioning, autoscale config, model hosting, and run weekly perf reports. (Primary: me)
- NovaTech: provide eval sets, procurement signoff, and any firewall/VPC contacts. (Primary: Samira)

Attachments: I attached the poc-sizing.xlsx and a short workload report export you shared on the call.

Next steps: can you confirm if the burst tolerance to 6 GPUs is acceptable and whether procurement can sign the SOW this week? If yes I’ll send an updated SOW and a drive link with the infra checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Forwarding Samira's confirmation — adding a few infra notes from the engineering side:

- Spin-up: for Reserved + Burst we can pre-warm a small standby pool (1 GPU) so demo spikes see ~30-60s cold-start for additional GPUs depending on cloud provider; full warm state (model weights + KV cache) ~3-5 min unless we pre-cache.
- Memory: for long-sequence summaries we recommend one H100-class or 2x A100-80GB config to keep batched latency <2s. If NovaTech prefers A100-only, we can shard across 2x A100-80GB.
- Autoscale policy: suggest threshold-based scaling on concurrent requests + CPU/GPU utilization with a minimum cooldown window of 90s and max scale step of +2 GPUs per minute to avoid oscillation.
- Logging/metrics: include token-level cost, 95/99 latency, and queue depth metrics to the Redwood Console.

I’ll draft a short POC infra diagram and proposed autoscale policy to attach to the SOW.

-Aisha
Solutions Engineer, Redwood

Committed-hours estimate (4-week POC):

- Burst: We’ll include a burst pool up to +4 GPUs for demo days; estimate 8 demo hours total over 4 weeks -> ~32 GPU-hours of burst (billed at burst rate).
- Total example billable hours: 1376 GPU-hours (baseline + expected burst). Exact dollar amounts will be in the SOW pricing table; I’ll include low/medium/high scenarios.

Data handling / SOC2 note:
- Redwood Private control plane can be deployed with VPC peering; by default input data and logs remain in your VPC and do not leave your cloud region.
